description:
Found while building bd-4et (bn daemon stop/restart). PRE-EXISTING and affects
EVERY subcommand, not just daemon.

    $ bn --json daemon stop
    error: unrecognized subcommand 'stop'

Cause: the global flag is declared `--json [<JSON>]` — an OPTIONAL value. So clap
happily eats the next token as that value: `--json` takes `daemon` as its
argument, and then `stop` is left dangling as an unknown top-level subcommand.

Works fine:
    bn daemon stop --json        (flag after the subcommand)
    bn --json=true daemon stop   (value glued on with =)

Why it matters: `--json` reads as a global flag (it IS declared globally, and it
is listed in every subcommand's help), so putting it first is the natural thing
to type — and the error you get back names the wrong problem entirely. It says
"unrecognized subcommand 'stop'", which sends you looking for a typo in the
subcommand instead of at the flag. Confusing sia.

Options:
  1. Make it a plain `bool` flag (`--json` with no value, `SetTrue`). Cleanest,
     matches how every other CLI does it, and `--json=true` can stay working via
     `num_args(0..=1)` + `default_missing_value`. NOTE: check the compat surface
     first — the `[possible values: true, false]` in the help suggests something
     out there may pass an explicit value positionally.
  2. Keep the optional value but set `require_equals(true)`, so a bare `--json`
     cannot consume the next token.

(2) is the smaller change and fixes the reported symptom exactly. (1) is what a
user expects. Either way, add a test that `bn --json <subcommand>` parses.
title: kopi-beans: global '--json' before a subcommand swallows it ('bn --json daemon stop' fails)

description:
GH: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/4
Part of the CJK / annotated-PDF field report (2026-08-01), epic bd-ski.
Original write-up: docs/issues/field-report-2026-08-01/

--- original GH body, verbatim ---


> Part of the **pdf2md CJK/annotated-PDF** work order — see the tracking issue for shared context, the corrections in §0, and the additive-corruption principle these cards rest on.

**Confidence:** High. **Owns:** `crates/kopitiam-document/src/validation/{mod.rs,report.rs}`

## Problem

`729152` emits runs of `���` and scores `recovery_ratio: 1.0`, `passes: true`.

U+FFFD is a legitimate graceful fallback at the font layer (`crates/kopitiam-pdf/src/mupdf/font.rs:554`) — a CID→Unicode lookup miss, not a crash. But by the time a document is **rendered**, a page dense in replacement characters is a failed page, and nothing says so.

## Change

Compute replacement-character density per page (count of U+FFFD ÷ content chars). Surface in `ConversionReport` per page and document-wide.

Gate: any nonzero count emits a warning; above a threshold (suggest 1% of a page's content chars, tunable) the page fails and the document does not `PASS`.

Per §2.4 this must be an **absolute** property of the rendered side — do **not** implement as an extracted-vs-rendered comparison, which cancels out.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Synthetic fixture: a `Page` of spans where 5% of characters are `\u{FFFD}` → document does not pass; report names the page.
- [ ] Negative fixture: clean page with a single legitimate `\u{FFFD}` in body text → warns, does not fail.
- [ ] Existing tests in `validation/mod.rs` (`dropped_content_fails`, `repaired_hyphenation_still_passes`, …) pass unchanged.
- [ ] Real corpus: `729152` no longer reports `PASS`.

title: [pdf2md] F-1 — Validation: detect substitutive corruption (U+FFFD density)
